thingsToDo.title: Explore National Elk Refuge
thingsToDo.description: The National Elk Refuge was established in 1912 just northeast of Jackson to protect winter habitat for the Jackson elk herd in the southern Greater Yellowstone ecosystem. The refuge encompasses about 24,700 acres of valley floor and foothill terrain and is managed by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Seasonal migration patterns bring thousands of elk into the area each winter, and long-term management includes habitat restoration, conflict mitigation, and coordination with nearby Grand Teton National Park. Because the refuge directly borders the town, it provides a clear example of wildlife conservation operating next to a major tourism gateway. Its acreage, founding year, and federal designation make it one of Jackson’s defining public lands.
